subject: CRTE
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: CRTE
courses.title: Understanding Creative Technologies
courses.description: Offers students an opportunity to engage with the communicative and ethical dimensions of new technology through a combination of empirical analysis and problem solving. Organized into four units that collectively present an interdisciplinary approach to media and technology in the 21st century. Begins with a technology-focused unit that emphasizes how social and cultural contexts shape how machines function and how people interact with them. Continues with units concerning digital media and design and audience that introduce the creation of media content through a critical lens. Concludes with a unit on ethics that asks students to reflect on the ethical dimensions of the decisions and problem solving highlighted in previous units.

courses.subject: CRTE
courses.title: Developing Creative Technologies
courses.description: Explores tools, processes, and technologies to develop human-centered prototype experiences with creative technologies. Offers students an opportunity to learn, use, experiment with, and test creative technologies using prototype scopes ranging from rapid and paper prototypes to mid- and high-fidelity prototypes. Also offers choice of technology based on student interest. Students share and learn through critique and user testing from interdisciplinary feedback to improve their prototype projects.

courses.subject: CRTE
courses.title: Creative Technologies Studio
courses.description: Focuses on the design of experiences and artifacts using creative technologies starting with concepts and culminating with a usable project. Students utilize multiple ideation methods to develop their project ideas. Once ideas have been cultivated, students work individually or as part of a small group to bring their project to fruition. Students work in critical groups to strengthen project ideas, prototype them using current hardware and software to collect meaningful feedback, and iterate to improve the project. Designed to illustrate the need for rapid innovation, resiliency, and gracefulness in the face of frequent failure situations.

courses.subject: CRTE
courses.title: Creative Technologies Project
courses.description: Offers students an opportunity to create a culminating project that builds upon the studio course project and aligns with their chosen concentration and professional aspirations. Students work individually or as part of a small group to outline a proposal to guide the planning and design of the project that will serve as the cornerstone of their portfolio. Weekly work results in a formal prototype, written report, and final presentation that discusses and reflects on the design process at the crossroads of methodological, systematic iteration and creative exploration.
